In the permanganate ion ($\text{MnO}_4^-$), the manganese atom is in the +7 oxidation state. The electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}^{7+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^0$.

Because the central metal ion has a $d^0$ configuration, there are no electrons in the $3d$ orbitals. Ligand-field parameters such as $Dq$ (the crystal field splitting parameter) and $B$ (the Racah parameter) are used to describe the energy levels and electronic transitions (d-d transitions) of electrons within the $d$-shell. Since there are no $d$-electrons, d-d transitions are impossible.

The observed absorption bands at 17,570, 31,560, and 38,320 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ have very high molar extinction coefficients ($\epsilon \approx 1,500\text{--}3,000 \text{ M}^{-1}\text{cm}^{-1}$), which is characteristic of allowed transitions. Specifically, these are Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer (LMCT) transitions, where an electron is promoted from a predominantly oxygen $2p$ orbital to a manganese $3d$ orbital. 

Because these bands arise from charge transfer rather than d-d transitions, they cannot be used to determine the ligand-field splitting parameter $Dq$ or the Racah parameter $B$ within the framework of ligand-field theory for $d^n$ complexes.
